terms.comment: Classically a master or owner; in the Vulgate and the Church God (Greek Κύριος) and Christ (Lewis & Short). The vocative is Domine; Dominus noster, Our Lord.

phrases.latin: Dominus regit mē, et nihil mihi deerit
phrases.english: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall want nothing

phrases.latin: Vōs vocātis mē Magister et Domine, et bene dīcitis: sum etenim.
phrases.english: You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right, for so I am.

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-vulgata), checked against the editions named there.
Vulgate verses checked against the Clementine Vulgate (CrossWire VulgClementine, via the scrollmapper bible_databases repository) and Hetzenauer’s edition, in Clementine spelling.
